arxiv-2206-08870.title: The Pixel Luminosity Telescope: A detector for luminosity measurement at CMS using silicon pixel sensors
arxiv-2206-08870.creator: The CMS BRIL Collaboration
arxiv-2206-08870.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by The CMS BRIL Collaboration. The Pixel Luminosity Telescope is a silicon pixel detector dedicated to luminosity measurement at the CMS experiment at the LHC. It is located approximately 1.75 \unit m from the interaction point and arranged into 16 “telescopes”, with eight telescopes installed around the beam pipe at either end of the detector and each telescope composed of three individual silicon sensor planes.

arxiv-2407-14142.title: Early Preparation Pays Off: New Classifier Pre-tuning for Class Incremental Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2407-14142.creator: Zhengyuan Xie, Haiquan Lu, Jia-wen Xiao, Enguang Wang, Le Zhang, Xialei Liu (🖂)
arxiv-2407-14142.description: Abstract Class incremental semantic segmentation aims to preserve old knowledge while learning new tasks, however, it is impeded by catastrophic forgetting and background shift issues. Prior works indicate the pivotal importance of initializing new classifiers and mainly focus on transferring knowledge from the background classifier or preparing classifiers for future classes, neglecting the flexibility and variance of new classifiers.

arxiv-2505-21484.title: A fixed-point theorem for face maps, or deleting entries in random finite sets
arxiv-2505-21484.creator: Tom Hutchcroft, Nicolas Monod, Omer Tamuz
arxiv-2505-21484.description: Abstract . We establish a fixed-point theorem for the face maps that consist in deleting the i i th entry of an ordered set. Furthermore, we show that there exists random finite sets of integers that are almost invariant under such deletions. 1. Introduction Results Consider a finite set E of integers.

arxiv-2506-02387.title: VS-Bench : Evaluating VLMs for Strategic Reasoning and Decision-Making in Multi-Agent Environments
arxiv-2506-02387.creator: Zelai Xu, Zhexuan Xu, Xiangmin Yi, Huining Yuan, Xinlei Chen, Yi Wu, Chao Yu, Yu Wang
arxiv-2506-02387.description: Abstract Recent advancements in Vision Language Models (VLMs) have expanded their capabilities to interactive agent tasks, yet existing benchmarks remain limited to single-agent or text-only environments. In contrast, real-world scenarios often involve multiple agents interacting within rich visual and linguistic contexts, posing challenges with both multimodal observations and strategic interactions.

arxiv-2507-04487.title: LoSiA: Efficient High-Rank Fine-Tuning via Subnet Localization and Optimization
arxiv-2507-04487.creator: Xujia Wang Yunjia Qi Bin Xu
arxiv-2507-04487.description: Abstract Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) methods, such as LoRA, significantly reduce the number of trainable parameters by introducing low-rank decomposition matrices. However, existing methods perform extensive matrix multiplications in domain specialization tasks, resulting in computational inefficiency and sub-optimal fine-tuning performance. Hence, we propose LoSiA 1 1 1 The source code is released at https://github.com/KlozeWang/LoSiA .

arxiv-2510-23088.title: Machine Learning approach to modeling of neutral particles transport in plasma Journal: Contributions to Plasma Physics
arxiv-2510-23088.creator: M.V. Umansky, G.J. Parker, R.D. Smirnov
arxiv-2510-23088.description: Abstract A propagator-based approach is investigated for Monte-Carlo (MC) modeling of neutral particles transport in fusion boundary plasmas. The propagator is essentially a Green’s function for the neutral kinetic equation, which depends on the plasma profiles. A Neural Network (NN) based model for the propagator provides a fast and accurate solution for the neutral distribution function in plasma.

pmc-11355164.title: Bone Health Optimization in Adult Spinal Deformity Patients: A Narrative Review
pmc-11355164.creator: Yousef A Al-Najjar, Danyal A Quraishi, Neerav Kumar, Ibrahim Hussain, Hiroyuki Katoh
pmc-11355164.description: Osteoporosis and low bone mineral density (BMD) pose significant challenges in adult spinal deformity surgery, increasing the risks of complications such as vertebral compression fractures, hardware failure, proximal junctional kyphosis/failure, and pseudoarthrosis. This narrative review examines the current evidence on bone health optimization strategies for spinal deformity patients.

pmc-11399652.title: Approaching a cure for nasopharyngeal carcinoma: how close are we from there?
pmc-11399652.creator: Victor Ho-Fun Lee
pmc-11399652.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). e diseases while radical concurrent chemoradiation is indicated for locoregionally advanced diseases. pmc-11425463.title: 214 Moving Forward - Exercise Promotion At A Major Trauma Centre
pmc-11425463.creator: Ruairi Connolly, Eanna MacSuibhne, Sinead Long, Michael Dunphy, Stephen Halpin
pmc-11425463.description: PurposeReturning to exercise after traumatic injuries is essential. Regular movement plays a crucial role in rehabilitation and long-term health. Returning to exercise post trauma can be difficult due to new impairment, pain and fear of re-injury. With our initiative – Moving Forward – we aimed to integrate exercise promotion into care provision at a major trauma centre.

pmc-12397374.title: Acoustic generation of orbital currents
pmc-12397374.creator: Mari Taniguchi, Satoshi Haku, Hyun-Woo Lee, Kazuya Ando
pmc-12397374.description: In solids, the crystal field couples the electronic orbital degree of freedom to the lattice. This coupling suggests that an excitation of lattice dynamics could trigger the dynamics of orbital angular momentum of electrons, thereby generating orbital currents—a flow of electronic orbital angular momentum. However, the interplay between orbital currents and lattice dynamics has been elusive.

pmc-12470457.title: Ablative Techniques for the Management of Osseous Spine Metastases: A Narrative Review
pmc-12470457.creator: Zach Pennington, Jonathan M Morris, Aladine Elsamadicy, Sheng-Fu Larry Lo, Joseph H Schwab, Daniel M Sciubba, Aldo Spallone, Se-Jun Park
pmc-12470457.description: With continued improvements in systemic cancer therapies, there has been an increase in the survivorship of patients with spinal metastases. However, many patients with spinal metastases are frail and may not be able to tolerate the morbidity of open surgery. For these patients, percutaneous ablation techniques offer a minimally invasive approach that can facilitate local tumor control and pain relief.

pmc-12554405.title: Age and Health Status Benefits Following Initiation of Atrial Fibrillation‐Specific Treatments
pmc-12554405.creator: Ryo Nakamaru, Nobuhiro Ikemura, Shun Kohsaka, Takehiro Kimura, Yoshinori Katsumata, Takahiko Nishiyama, Ikuko Ueda, Kojiro Tanimoto, Koji Negishi, Seiji Takatsuki, John A Spertus, Masaki Ieda
pmc-12554405.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAtrial fibrillation (AF) is managed with various strategies, including rate and rhythm control, to improve patients' health status. Although its incidence increases with age, how age affects health status improvements following AF treatment remains unknown.MethodsUsing data from a multicenter registry for outpatients with newly recognized AF, baseline and 1‐year health status was assessed with the Atrial Fibrillation Effect on Quality‐of‐life quesTionnaire (AFEQT).

pmc-12751967.title: Effects of emotion-oriented interventions on cognitive, behavioral, and psychological symptoms in people with dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
pmc-12751967.creator: Andrea Duarte-Díaz, Yolanda Álvarez-Pérez, Vanesa Ramos-García, Lilisbeth Perestelo-Pérez, Marta Aymerich, Noemí Robles, Carme Carrion
pmc-12751967.description: BackgroundDementia is a major global health challenge associated with progressive cognitive decline and neuropsychiatric symptoms that greatly affect patients and caregivers. Emotion-oriented interventions (EOIs) are nonpharmacological approaches designed to address not only cognitive deficits but also the emotional and psychological needs of people with dementia.

pmc-12986987.title: qAG2.1 Is Associated with Anaerobic Germination Tolerance in Rice Seeds: Evidence from Haplotype Analysis and Marker-Assisted Breeding
pmc-12986987.creator: Vijay Kumar Reddy Challa, Siddharth Panda, Annamalai Anandan, Sharat Kumar Pradhan, Aruna Yelemele Raghavendra Rao, Bhojaraja Naik Keshava
pmc-12986987.description: Anaerobic germination tolerance (AGT) is a critical adaptive trait for rice establishment in flood-prone environments and direct-seeded systems. Here, we identified and validated the quantitative trait locus qAG2.1 for AGT and introgressed it into the elite lowland rice variety CR Dhan 801 through marker-assisted backcross breeding.

pmc-13040024.title: A low-complexity compact dual-polarized patch antenna with high isolation and low cross-polarization for in-band full-duplex applications
pmc-13040024.creator: Hung Tran-Huy, Trang Hoang-Thu, Tu Le-Tuan, Mohammad Alibakhshikenari, Yazeed Mohammad Qasaymeh, Takfarinas Saber, Patrizia Livreri
pmc-13040024.description: This paper proposes a simple design of a dual-polarized microstrip patch antenna featuring compact dimensions, low cross-polarization, and high port isolation, specifically designed for full-duplex wireless applications. The antenna is implemented on a single-layer substrate, and size reduction is achieved through a capacitive loading technique. Additionally, capacitive loading also contributes to increasing polarization purity by suppressing cross-polarization radiation.

pmc-13143413.title: Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation Haemoperfusion for Leptospirosis Pulmonary Hemorrhagic Disease: Report of 1 Case
pmc-13143413.creator: Qigang Zeng, Longyun Xie, Wenshan Dai, Feilong Xu, Yong Dai
pmc-13143413.description: Severe pulmonary leptospirosis (SPFL), characterized by diffuse alveolar haemorrhage (DAH) and acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), carries a high mortality, often due to diagnostic delays and complex management. We report a case of a 42‐year‐old male with outdoor occupational exposure who presented with fever and hemoptysis, rapidly progressing to severe respiratory failure and thrombocytopenia. Chest imaging confirmed DAH/ARDS.

pmc-13196172.title: Association of iliopsoas muscle cross-sectional area with postoperative complications in older lung cancer patients: a retrospective study
pmc-13196172.creator: Shoko Kubota, Joji Samejima, Yutaro Koike, Makoto Tada, Tomohiro Miyoshi, Kenta Tane, Masashi Wakabayashi, Keiju Aokage, Masahiro Tsuboi
pmc-13196172.description: BackgroundSarcopenia was correlated with increased postoperative complications and poor outcomes in patients with lung cancer. The cross-sectional area of the iliopsoas muscle on computed tomography is a relevant indicator of sarcopenia. This study aimed to investigate whether the preoperative cross-sectional area of the iliopsoas muscle is associated with the incidence of postoperative complications after lobectomy.

pmc-13411787.title: Combined pancreatic grade 1 neuroendocrine tumour and ductal adenocarcinoma — MiNEN versus collision tumour: a rare surgical case report and diagnostic challenge
pmc-13411787.creator: Noufel Alshadood, Suha Hazem Yasir, Ali Naser Aldarawsha, Flayyih Hasan Yousif, Mohamed Samy Elazab, Sora Ali Hasan, Hasan Ammash, Mustafa Nabeel Mahmood

pmc-13521462.title: Continuous Purification of mRNA Produced by In Vitro Transcription Using High Performance Countercurrent Membrane Purification
pmc-13521462.creator: Ziqiao Wang, Amin Javidanbardan, Ali Behboudi, Andrew L Zydney
pmc-13521462.description: Messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA) therapeutics produced by in vitro transcription must be purified to remove residual enzymes and free nucleotides. This study examines the use of high‐performance countercurrent membrane purification (HPCMP) for the purification of mRNA therapeutics based on differences in the rate of diffusion across semipermeable polyethersulfone hollow fiber membranes.

pmc-13588562.title: Temporal changes in rabies epidemiology in Brazil: an analysis of notifications of suspected and confirmed human rabies cases, 2010-2025
pmc-13588562.creator: João Vitor Engelhardt, Halana do Carmo Silva, Gabriel Campana do Nascimento, Arthur Moraes Lavinas, Beatriz Biancardi de Campos, Eduarda Scárdua Coser, Bruno Vidal Boscaglia, Elinara Ferreira Santos, Sarah Fernandes Teixeira, Mariana Rambaldi do Nascimento, Joamyr Victor Rossoni, Clairton Marcolongo
pmc-13588562.description: Human rabies is an invariably fatal encephalitis caused by Lyssavirus species, with near-100% lethality after symptom onset. In Brazil, canine vaccination has markedly reduced urban transmission. However, human deaths continue to occur and are increasingly linked to sylvatic reservoirs, particularly Desmodus rotundus bats.

pmc-13627270.title: Inhibition of pancreatic cancer growth by an siRNA targeting SNORA22 and a folic acid-conjugated cationic oligopeptide
pmc-13627270.creator: Kazuhiro Hiyama, Miki Nishigawa, Kazunori Takagi, Kazuki Sato, Rintaro Iwata Hara, Kaoru Furihata, Kazushige Uchida, Takeshi Wada, Keisuke Taniuchi

pmc-13660868.title: Association between Yo-yo intermittent recovery test, physiological markers of endurance performance, and buffering capacity in professional soccer players
pmc-13660868.creator: R.C.A. Ferreira, V.O. Silvino, L.V. Vilhena, M.A.P. dos Santos, D.M.L. do Prado
pmc-13660868.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The Yo-Yo Intermittent Recovery Test Level 1 (YYIR1) is widely recognized as a reliable tool for assessing intermittent endurance and aerobic capacity in team sports athletes. This study aims to verify the association between YYIR1 and physiological markers of endurance performance in professional soccer players, as well as the relationship between metabolic buffering capacity, metabolic acidosis tolerance, and YYIR1 total distance.

pmc-13683027.title: Hypertension and pain: A state-based framework for cardiovascular–nociceptive coupling
pmc-13683027.creator: Basak Donertas-Ayaz, Carlos J Cruz, John K Neubert, Robert M Caudle
pmc-13683027.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Experimental and epidemiological studies suggest that blood pressure (BP)-pain associations vary across normotension, hypertension, and chronic pain, but the mechanisms underlying these differences remain unclear. In pain-free individuals, higher resting BP is often associated with lower experimental pain sensitivity. Similar hypoalgesia is reported in some normotensive individuals with familial hypertension risk and in established hypertension, suggesting that reduced pain sensitivity is unlikely to be attributable to elevated BP alone.
